clue.text: Lord's guard hit hard with chair support

definitions.note: a batsman's guard is the stance taken against the stumps; Lord's is the London cricket ground

parts.note: in cricket, to middle the ball is to strike it cleanly with the middle of the bat
with and 'and' both mean together alongside
a leg holds up a chair

explanation.surface: Someone guarding themselves with a chair and lashing out hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is London's famous cricket ground, so 'Lord's guard' points to cricket: a batsman takes guard by lining the bat up against particular stumps, and one common position takes its name from two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking guard between the middle and leg stumps is a standard batting position, so it is a guard taken at a cricket ground like Lord's.

clue.text: Token note the French sent north

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A musician sends a token note northwards to the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent north' reverses only LA, giving AL; the note MINIM reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: A token gesture is a minimal one, the smallest amount offered.

clue.text: Dilettantes chucking out 50 ink- pads

indicators.note: throwing out tells us a letter is removed from the word for amateurs

parts.note: dabblers are amateurs who play at a subject
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Amateur artists throw away fifty ink pads.
explanation.definitionFit: Dabbers are pads used by printers and engravers to spread ink over a surface.

clue.text: See 9
Late start for lucky creature in prestigious meeting

indicators.note: late here means dead or gone, so the word loses its starting letter

parts.note: a mascot is an animal or figure kept to bring good luck

explanation.surface: A team's lucky mascot shows up late at a grand event.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is a famous, upmarket horse-race meeting in Berkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ascot races are one of the grandest fixtures in the British racing and social calendar.

clue.text: Shattering some old ash in grove

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ancient ash tree in a wood is being split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash hopes is to wreck them, so dashing can mean destroying or smashing.

clue.text: Greek girl drops ecstasy in claret when sloshed

indicators.note: in places the single drug letter within the jumbled wine letters it is dropped into
sloshed means drunk, so the wine's letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: to drop a pill is slang for taking it, and E is the usual abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A Greek woman takes a drug in red wine once she's drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when sloshed' scrambles CLARET to ELCTRA, and 'in' places E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is a daughter of Agamemnon in Greek myth and tragedy.

clue.text: This is said to be the precursor of a swallow

definitions.text: This is said to be the precursor of a swallow

parts.words: This is said to be the precursor of a swallow
parts.note: a toast spoken just before gulping a drink; swallow pretends to be the bird

explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' suggests the bird, and 'precursor' some earlier species, but it is a gulp of drink, and the phrase is a toast people say before downing one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a cheery drinking toast said just before knocking back a drink.

clue.text: Passenger vehicle's bumper

definitions.meaning: the full original name for a bus
an extra-large edition, as of a book or TV programme collecting several parts

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the old term for a bus and also describes a volume or broadcast gathering many episodes.

clue.text: Star student class involved in massacre

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A top pupil's class takes part in a slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: All sixteen letters of 'Star student class' are rearranged by 'involved'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of the Little Bighorn in 1876, where the US cavalry commander and his men were wiped out, is remembered by this phrase.

clue.text: Woman perished at sea having eaten soft food

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: having eaten means the jumbled letters take another letter inside them
at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled into a new order

parts.note: P stands for piano, soft in music

explanation.surface: A woman lost at sea had eaten something soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges PERISHED to PHERDSIE, and 'having eaten' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This British dish is minced lamb baked under a mashed potato crust.

clue.text: Holy book for cardinals?

definitions.meaning: the fourth book of the Old Testament
the question mark nods to the churchmen

explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's fourth book has this title, and cardinals are counting figures as opposed to ordinals.

clue.text: Degraded silt that chokes the plant

indicators.note: to choke something is to grip it round the neck, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: degraded means broken down, so the letters of silt are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eroded silt smothers a garden plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degraded' rearranges the silt to ISTL, and 'chokes' means the word 'the' wraps around those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This prickly flowering weed is Scotland's national emblem.

clue.text: Scrapes cavities

definitions.meaning: awkward fixes or predicaments, as in being in a spot of bother

explanation.definitionFit: Being in a tight spot is being in a hole, and hollows dug in the ground are also called this.

clue.text: Car diagram shows what fan may require

parts.note: auto is a short word for a motor car
a graph is a chart or diagram

explanation.surface: A drawing of a car tells you what an enthusiast is after.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirers ask celebrities for a signature, which is what they hope to take home.

clue.text: Dog or elephant worker leaving in temper

definitions.note: dog and bone is Cockney rhyming slang for a phone

indicators.note: in puts the shortened animal inside the word for temper

parts.note: to tone something is to moderate or temper it

indicators.note: leaving means that part walks out of the animal's name

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A dog or an elephant handler storms off in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, a London working-class idiom, uses 'dog and bone' for a phone, shortened to 'dog'. 'leaving' drops ANT from ELEPHANT to leave ELEPH.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang the phone is called the dog, so a dog here is the device you ring people on.

clue.text: Murderous house police to probe encrypted mail

indicators.note: probing means pushing into something, so the police letters go inside
encrypted means scrambled into code, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Police search a house over coded mail about a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encrypted' turns MAIL into MIAL, and 'to probe' sends CID into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Homicide is killing, so something given to it is bloodthirsty and deadly.

clue.text: Gas will give shivering men heat

indicators.note: shivering means shaking, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Gas heating will warm up cold men.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the main component of natural gas used for heating and cooking.

clue.text: Two containers on a Spanish saloon bar

parts.note: a can and a tin are both metal containers, side by side

explanation.surface: Two drinks cans on the counter in a Spanish pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantina is a bar or tavern in Spain and Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Support holding piano for this player

indicators.note: holding means the support wraps around the single letter

parts.note: a pier is a pillar holding up a bridge or arch
P is the musical abbreviation for piano

explanation.surface: A stand holding a piano for the performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A piper plays the bagpipes or a pipe, a musician.

clue.text: Old songwriter exiles son, one given lines to read

indicators.note: exiles means sends away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a psalmist wrote the Psalms, such as King David

explanation.surface: An ancient composer banishes his son, who is handed some lines to learn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' suggests an actor's script, but they are the lines on a palm.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune-teller who reads the lines on hands for a living.

clue.text: Cleric fills bucket to prove superior

indicators.note: fills means the cleric goes inside the bucket

parts.note: a pail is a bucket
Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric

explanation.surface: A vicar fills a bucket to show he is better than others.
explanation.definitionFit: To win out or triumph over rivals is to come out on top.

clue.text: Dicky ate nuts getting lockjaw

indicators.note: dicky means weak or faulty, so these letters are out of order

explanation.surface: Someone with a dodgy stomach ate nuts and got a nasty disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Lockjaw is the common name for this bacterial infection that stiffens the jaw muscles.

clue.text: View the place we're told

indicators.note: we're told means the word is heard spoken rather than seen

parts.note: a site is the place where something is

explanation.surface: We hear that this is the spot for a view.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or spectacle, as in a sight for sore eyes.

clue.text: Weight-lifters' stretches keeping you back

definitions.note: plural noun, the 's links to the wordplay as 'is'

indicators.note: keeping means one word holds the other inside

parts.note: pulls means strains or stretches, as with muscles

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: ye is old-fashioned for you

explanation.surface: Gym weightlifters stretching keep you back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the old word for you round to EY. The definition is cryptic: these are devices that lift weights, not gym-goers.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheel with a rope over it is used to hoist heavy loads.

clue.text: Ambassador leads a consortium in enquiry

indicators.note: leads means comes in front of the rest

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
a ring is a group or cartel working together

explanation.surface: A diplomat heads a business group in an investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal inquiry, such as a court or tribunal session, is called this.

clue.text: Oriental art fiddle old Parisian chum conceals

indicators.note: conceals means the outer letters hide the other word inside

parts.note: ami is French for friend
to rig is to fiddle or fix dishonestly

explanation.surface: An old French friend hides a fiddle involving Eastern art.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper folding is the traditional Japanese craft.

clue.text: Go out to lunch as an office?

definitions.note: an adjective: relating to a section of an organisation

parts.note: to depart is to go
slang for crazy or mad

explanation.surface: Leaving to eat as an office does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out to lunch' reads like a lunch break; it splits as 'Go' plus 'out to lunch', meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: An office may be a department of a larger body, so things concerning it are of a division.
